glance_notes.source_name: Nebraska Secretary of State — 2026 Official Election Calendar
glance_notes.text: 2026 General Election Registration Deadlines: For Nebraska's November 3, 2026 General Election, mail, online, DMV and certain other voter registration methods close on October 16. Eligible residents may continue registering in person at their county election office through 6:00 p.m. on October 23.

glance_notes.source_name: Nebraska Secretary of State — Early Voting
glance_notes.text: No-Excuse Early Voting: Nebraska allows any registered voter to vote early without providing an excuse. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, regular early-voting ballots are ready for mailing by September 28 and in-person early voting begins October 5. November 2 is the final day to vote early in person.

glance_notes.source_name: Nebraska Secretary of State — Voter ID
glance_notes.text: Photo ID Required: Nebraska requires registered voters, with limited exceptions, to provide acceptable photo identification when voting. A voter who has a reasonable impediment to presenting acceptable photo ID may use Nebraska's reasonable impediment certification process.

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: Eligible Nebraska residents may register online through NEReg2Vote, in person at their county election office, through the Department of Motor Vehicles and certain other state agencies, or by submitting a voter registration application by mail. There is no waiting period after becoming a Nebraska resident before registering. To vote, a person must be a U.S. citizen, a Nebraska resident and at least 18 years old by Election Day. A person convicted of a felony cannot register or vote until completing the sentence, including any probation or parole term. A person found by a court to be mentally incompetent cannot register while that disqualification remains in effect.
register.glance_value: Online, mail, county office or designated agencies
register.source_name: Nebraska Secretary of State — Registering to Vote
register.internal_note: The Secretary of State directly confirms NEReg2Vote, county election office registration, DMV registration and registration through certain state agencies. The current official guidance states there is no Nebraska-residency waiting period. The felony rule requires completion of the sentence including probation or parole before registration. First-time Nebraska voters registering by mail should provide the identification documentation described by the state to avoid delays.

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Use Nebraska's official Voter Information Center to check your voter registration status. The system also provides voter-specific election information and can be used to track the status of an early-voting ballot.
check_registration.glance_value: Check through the Voter Information Center
check_registration.source_name: Nebraska Secretary of State — Voter Information Center
check_registration.internal_note: The Secretary of State's registration and early-voting materials direct voters to VoterCheck/VoterView for registration and early-ballot information. County election offices remain the authoritative local contact if information is missing or incorrect.

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: For Nebraska's November 3, 2026 General Election, voter registrations submitted by mail must be postmarked by October 16. October 16 is also the deadline for registrations completed through the Department of Motor Vehicles and for registrations delivered by personal messenger or personal agent. Eligible residents may register in person at their County Clerk or Election Commissioner's office through 6:00 p.m. on Friday, October 23. Nebraska does not provide general Election Day voter registration.
deadlines.source_name: Nebraska Secretary of State — 2026 Official Election Calendar
deadlines.internal_note: Nebraska's general rule places mail, DMV and certain other registration deadlines on the third Friday before an election and permits in-person county-office registration through 6:00 p.m. on the second Friday before the election. For November 3, 2026, those dates are October 16 and October 23. There are narrow statutory exceptions for certain recently naturalized citizens, former federal employees and presidential-only voters, but these do not constitute general Election Day registration.

polling_place.label: Find a Polling Place
polling_place.content: Use Nebraska's official Voter Information Center to find voter-specific Election Day information, including the polling place assigned to your registration. Because polling locations can change, voters should verify their location before Election Day or contact their county election office. Eleven Nebraska counties currently conduct all elections entirely by mail, so voters in those counties automatically receive ballots rather than using ordinary precinct polling places. A voter in a by-mail precinct who wants to vote in person may vote at the county election official's office on Election Day.
polling_place.glance_value: Check the Voter Information Center; 11 counties vote by mail
polling_place.source_name: Nebraska Secretary of State — Election Day FAQ
polling_place.internal_note: Important Nebraska distinction: the Secretary of State currently identifies Boone, Cedar, Cherry, Clay, Dawes, Dixon, Garden, Knox, Merrick, Morrill and Stanton as counties conducting all elections completely by mail. Voters in by-mail precincts may still vote in person at the county election official's office on Election Day. This should not be presented as if every Nebraska voter has a conventional assigned Election Day polling site.

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: Nebraska's Gubernatorial Statewide General Election is Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Polls are open from 8:00 a.m. until 8:00 p.m. Central Time and from 7:00 a.m. until 7:00 p.m. Mountain Time. Anyone who is in the polling place or in line when the polls close is entitled to vote. Nebraska requires acceptable photo identification for statewide elections, with limited exceptions and a reasonable impediment procedure. Eleven Nebraska counties currently conduct elections entirely by mail, although voters in by-mail precincts may vote in person at their county election official's office on Election Day.
election_day.source_name: Nebraska Secretary of State — Election Day FAQ
election_day.internal_note: Nebraska Revised Statute 32-908 directly establishes 8:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. in the Central Time Zone and 7:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m. in the Mountain Time Zone and protects voters already present or in line at closing. The Secretary of State's current Election Day FAQ confirms the same hours and the state's all-mail counties.

polling_hours.label: Polling Hours
polling_hours.content: Nebraska polling places are open from 8:00 a.m. until 8:00 p.m. in the Central Time Zone and from 7:00 a.m. until 7:00 p.m. in the Mountain Time Zone. Voters who are inside the polling place or waiting in line at the official closing time must be allowed enough time to vote.
polling_hours.internal_note: Nebraska spans Central and Mountain time zones. Revised Statute 32-908 expressly establishes both schedules and provides that polls remain open long enough for voters who were present or in line at the official closing hour to cast their ballots.

early_voting.label: Early In-Person Voting
early_voting.content: Nebraska is a no-excuse early-voting state, so any registered voter may vote early without providing a reason. For a statewide General Election, in-person early voting at county election offices begins 30 days before Election Day. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, that date is October 5. Monday, November 2 is the final day to cast an early ballot in person at the county election office. Office hours vary by county.
early_voting.source_name: Nebraska Secretary of State — Early Voting
early_voting.internal_note: The Secretary of State directly states that Nebraska is a no-excuse state, that in-person early voting for a statewide primary or general election begins 30 days before Election Day, and that the Monday before Election Day is the final day. The official 2026 calendar specifically lists November 2 as the final in-person early-voting day.

absentee_mail.label: Early Voting by Mail
absentee_mail.content: Any registered Nebraska voter may request an early-voting ballot by mail without providing an excuse. Applications may be submitted to the county election office by mail, fax or as a scanned or photographed signed application sent by email. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, regular early-voting ballots are ready for delivery by mail by September 28. The deadline for the county election office to receive an ordinary early-voting ballot application is 6:00 p.m. on Friday, October 23. Completed ballots must be received by the county election official by the close of polls on Election Day: 8:00 p.m. Central Time or 7:00 p.m. Mountain Time. Ballots may be returned by mail, personal delivery, agent, courier or an authorized county drop box.
absentee_mail.glance_value: No excuse required; request by 6:00 p.m. October 23
absentee_mail.source_name: Nebraska Secretary of State — Early Voting
absentee_mail.internal_note: The Secretary of State directly establishes no-excuse early voting, application methods, the second-Friday 6:00 p.m. application deadline and the Election Day receipt deadline. For November 3, the second Friday is October 23. The 2026 election calendar establishes September 28 as the deadline to have regular early-voting ballots ready for delivery by mail. Every Nebraska county currently maintains at least one secure ballot drop box.

voter_id.label: Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.content: Nebraska requires registered voters, with limited exceptions, to present an acceptable photo ID in every primary, general and special election. Accepted identification includes qualifying documents issued by the State of Nebraska, the federal government, the U.S. military, a Nebraska political subdivision, a Nebraska postsecondary institution or a recognized Nebraska tribal government. The ID may be expired, does not need to show an address and does not need an expiration date. A voter without acceptable photo ID at the polls may cast a provisional ballot and must present acceptable identification to the county election office in person on or before the Tuesday after the election for the ballot to count, unless the voter qualifies to use a reasonable impediment certification.
voter_id.glance_value: Photo ID required; reasonable impediment option available
voter_id.source_name: Nebraska Secretary of State — Voter ID
voter_id.internal_note: Nebraska's voter-ID requirement took effect with the May 2024 statewide primary. The Secretary of State directly states that acceptable IDs may be expired and need not contain an address or expiration date. An image or photocopy on a phone is not acceptable for in-person voting; the original ID must be presented. Voters without ID may cast a provisional ballot and cure it by the Tuesday after the election, while voters with qualifying reasonable impediments may use the certification procedure. UOCAVA voters have a limited exemption unless voting in person at a Nebraska polling site.

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: Nebraska provides accessible voting equipment and assistance for voters with disabilities. Voters who need help marking a ballot may receive assistance from a person of their choice, subject to federal restrictions, or from election workers. Nebraska polling locations must provide an accessible method for voters with disabilities to cast a ballot privately and independently. Voters who cannot sign an early-voting ballot return envelope because of a disability may use the assistance procedures provided by state law. Voters should contact their county election office before voting if they need a specific accommodation.
accessible_voting.glance_value: Accessible equipment and voter assistance available
accessible_voting.source_name: Nebraska Secretary of State — General Voter Information
accessible_voting.internal_note: The Secretary of State maintains dedicated Accessible Voting resources within General Voter Information. Nebraska's early-voting instructions also provide procedures when a voter needs assistance marking a ballot or cannot sign the return envelope. County election officials are the appropriate source for location-specific accessibility arrangements.

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: Nebraska provides special registration and early-voting procedures for eligible military members, qualifying family members and U.S. citizens living overseas. Covered voters may use the Federal Post Card Application to register and request a ballot. Nebraska also permits the Federal Write-In Absentee Ballot for registration and voting in federal, state and local elections. Military and overseas voters may track their ballots through the Voter Information Center. These voters should use Nebraska's dedicated military and overseas procedures because registration, identification and ballot-delivery rules can differ from the ordinary early-voting process.
military_overseas.glance_value: FPCA, FWAB and ballot tracking available
military_overseas.source_name: Nebraska Secretary of State — Military Voters
military_overseas.internal_note: The Secretary of State directly provides FPCA resources and confirms Nebraska's use of the FWAB for registration and voting in federal, state and local elections. The overseas-voter page is [https://sos.nebraska.gov/elections/overseas-voters](https://sos.nebraska.gov/elections/overseas-voters). Nebraska's voter-ID rules exempt active-duty military members, active-duty spouses and UOCAVA overseas voters from presenting photo ID unless they are registered Nebraska voters casting a ballot in person at a Nebraska polling site.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: A Nebraska resident who temporarily leaves home to attend college may remain registered in the home county. A student may instead register in the Nebraska county where the student attends college if that is the place the student intends to establish as a home and be habitually present. Declaring Nebraska residency for voting purposes does not change residency for tuition purposes. An out-of-state student attending school in Nebraska may continue voting in the student's home state if that remains the student's voting residence.
student_voting.glance_value: Students may use one qualifying home or college residence
student_voting.source_name: Nebraska Secretary of State — Student Voters
student_voting.internal_note: The Secretary of State's dedicated Student Voters page directly states that temporary college attendance does not require a Nebraska resident to change voting residence, permits registration in the college county when the student intends to establish a home and be habitually present there, and expressly states that voting residency does not alter tuition residency.

sample_ballot.label: Official Sample Ballot
sample_ballot.content: Nebraska publishes official sample ballots before statewide elections. State-level sample ballots show statewide contests, while voters who want a sample ballot containing contests specific to their address should contact their county election office. For the 2026 General Election, candidate, office and ballot-issue certification continues through September, so voters should check the Secretary of State and county election resources after ballots are finalized.
sample_ballot.internal_note: Nebraska's prior statewide sample-ballot pages explain that Secretary of State samples contain state-level contests and direct voters to county election offices for ballots containing local contests. The 2026 election page shows September 11 as the deadline for the Secretary of State to certify candidates, offices and issues to the statewide ballot. The 2026 calendar requires publication and distribution of sample ballots shortly before Election Day. Reverify after certification and publication of 2026 General Election samples.

contact.label: Contact the State Election Authority
contact.content: Nebraska Secretary of State, Elections Division, 1201 N Street, Suite 120, Lincoln, NE 68508. Toll-free elections phone: 888-727-0007. Email: sos.elect@nebraska.gov. For questions involving an individual voter registration, polling place, early-voting ballot or county-specific election procedure, contact the appropriate County Clerk or Election Commissioner.
contact.source_name: Nebraska Secretary of State — Elections Division
contact.internal_note: The Secretary of State's current military and overseas voter pages directly verify 888-727-0007 and [sos.elect@nebraska.gov](mailto:sos.elect@nebraska.gov). The email address is intentionally plain text with no Markdown or mailto wrapper. Nebraska's county election offices administer voter registration, polling locations and early voting locally.

official_resources.label: Official State & Local Resources
official_resources.content: Use the Nebraska Secretary of State Elections Division website for official statewide election information. Nebraska's Voter Information Center provides voter-specific registration and ballot information. County Clerks and Election Commissioners administer voter registration, early voting, ballot drop boxes, polling places and many other election functions locally.
official_resources.glance_value: Secretary of State, Voter Information Center & county offices
official_resources.internal_note: Official 2026 Election Calendar: [https://sos.nebraska.gov/sites/default/files/doc/elections/2026/2026_Election_Calendar.pdf](https://sos.nebraska.gov/sites/default/files/doc/elections/2026/2026_Election_Calendar.pdf). Official registration guidance: [https://sos.nebraska.gov/elections/registering-vote](https://sos.nebraska.gov/elections/registering-vote). Official Voter ID guidance: [https://sos.nebraska.gov/voter-id](https://sos.nebraska.gov/voter-id). Official military voting: [https://sos.nebraska.gov/elections/military-voters](https://sos.nebraska.gov/elections/military-voters). Official overseas voting: [https://sos.nebraska.gov/elections/overseas-voters](https://sos.nebraska.gov/elections/overseas-voters). Official student voting: [https://sos.nebraska.gov/elections/student-voters](https://sos.nebraska.gov/elections/student-voters).
